name: project-savannah-simulation
description: Build/test setup for the Australian Savannah predator-prey Java simulation (module_java)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project

The `module_java` worktrees contain a BlueJ-style predator-prey simulation (default package, no build file). Core model: `Actor` → `Consumer`/`Producer` → concrete species; `Field`/`Location` grid; `Simulator` orchestrates; `SimulatorView` (Swing) + `StatisticsView` (JavaFX).

**Build:** JavaFX is NOT installed in this environment, so `javac *.java` fails only on `Simulator.java` + `StatisticsView.java` (javafx imports). The model compiles cleanly. To get a full local compile, write minimal stub classes for the javafx symbols used and compile with `-cp <stubs>` — the rest of the project is plain Java/Swing/AWT.

**Deterministic testing:** `Randomizer` uses a fixed seed (10001) via `Randomizer.reset()`, so `Simulator.populate()` placement is reproducible and can be regression-hashed. Caveat: `Gender.getRandom()` uses `Math.random()` (NOT the seeded RNG), so exclude gender from any golden-value comparison.

**R003_module_java refactor done (2026-06-27): species registry.** This is a base-family variant (`Actor`→`Consumer`/`Producer`→species; seed 10001; Gender via Math.random()). `Simulator` previously kept species data in THREE parallel places (10 `*_CREATION_PROBABILITY` consts, 10 `*_COLOR` consts + 10 hardcoded `view.setColor(...)` calls, and a 10-branch if/else-if chain in `populate()` tagged `// Refactor this?`). Introduced new `SpeciesDescriptor.java` (class holding species `Class`, `Color`, creationProbability, + `@FunctionalInterface ActorFactory create(Field,Location)`) and a single `static final List<SpeciesDescriptor> SPECIES` (10 entries in population-priority order). populate() now loops SPECIES with `if(rand.nextDouble()<=d.getCreationProbability()){actors.add(d.create(...));break;}` — the for-loop-with-break is the exact desugaring of the cascade, so same nextDouble draw count/order per cell. Colour setup loops SPECIES then one explicit `view.setColor(Carcass.class, CARCASS_COLOR)` (carcasses are produced dynamically, not seeded → kept out of SPECIES). Adding a species = one list entry. **Verified behaviour-preserving:** standalone equivalence test (old if/else vs new loop) over all 19200 cells of the default 120×160 grid with `new Random(10001)` → 0 mismatches AND random stream stays aligned afterward (so any seeded populate() regression hash is unchanged). Full project compile-checked via a one-file `javafx.application.Application` stub + stub `StatisticsView` (only Simulator/StatisticsView need javafx). Did NOT fix the latent `depth<=0||depth<=0` width-validation bug at Simulator ctor (out of scope; doesn't affect default-size runs). **Dead code flagged but NOT removed (didn't author it):** `Animal.java`/`Rabbit.java`/`Fox.java` are a self-contained legacy foxes-and-rabbits cluster (`extends Animal`, `List<Animal>`), unreferenced by the active `Actor` hierarchy — recommended deletion to user. **UPDATE: user confirmed; `git rm`'d Animal.java/Rabbit.java/Fox.java (grep-verified zero remaining refs).** Then a second refactor: removed the do-nothing `act(List<Actor>)` overrides from ALL 10 concrete species (each just called `super.act(...)` — pure boilerplate; inherited Consumer.act/Producer.act runs identically, behaviour-preserving by language semantics, no RNG change). For the 3 producers (Acacia/StarGrass/RedOatGrass) this also let me drop their now-unused `import java.util.List;` + already-unused `Iterator`/`Random` imports. Consumers keep List/ArrayList imports (still used by `PREY = new ArrayList<>(List.of(...))`). Full project re-compiles clean via the javafx Application stub (32 classes). Third refactor (R003): dead-code removal in `Field.java` — grep-confirmed zero callers, removed `randomAdjacentLocation(Location)`, the entire `producerField` field + `createProducerField()` + `getProducerField()` cluster, the unused 3-arg `place(Object,int,int)` overload (only real caller Actor.java:119 uses the 2-arg Location version), and the unused `import java.util.Iterator`. Behaviour-preserving (none were invoked; `randomAdjacentLocation` would have consumed rand via shuffle but was never called). Recompiles clean (32 classes).

**R008_module_java variant (hierarchy: `LivingOrganism` → `Animal`(`Predator`/`Prey`)/`Plant` → Lion/Cheetah/Zebra/Giraffe/Lemur; Swing-only `SimulatorView`).** Compiles cleanly with plain `javac *.java` (the only javafx import in `Simulator.java` is COMMENTED OUT; just a JButton.setLabel deprecation note). KEY DIFFERENCE from other variants: `Randomizer.useShared = false`, so `getRandom()` returns a FRESH UNSEEDED `new Random()` each call — the sim is NON-deterministic across runs and `Randomizer.reset()` is a no-op. There are exactly 3 persistent generators (`LivingOrganism.rand`, `Field.rand`, `Weather.rand`, all `static final`) plus a local one in `Simulator.populate()`; no `Math.random()` anywhere. To verify behaviour-preserving refactors: reflectively `setSeed()` those 3 static-final Randoms (final blocks reassignment, not `setSeed` on the referenced object) BEFORE running, replicate `populate()`/`simulateOneStep()` in a view-free harness (the real view builds a JFrame → hangs headless), and FNV-hash a position-sensitive per-cell signature (animal class + infected + immune, plant presence). Comparison is valid because only the model classes differ between baseline/refactored runs. Latent quirk left as-is: `Animal.setDead()` has dead no-op code (`if (class==Lion||Cheetah) location=null;` after location already nulled).

**R008 refactors done (2026-06-26), all verified behaviour-preserving vs the pristine baseline commit 298c765 across 4 harness configs (default 60×90/120-step + seeds 11/7/5, steps up to 200, varied grids). Canonical fingerprints under the FINAL harness (seeds LivingOrganism=SEED, Field=SEED+1, Weather=SEED+2): default=-8651955994381610381, [150 11 22]=3170458861844968265, [200 7 99]=7234180482974749471, [120 5 5 80 120]=-422301020194460238.** Harness lives at /tmp/harness/Harness.java (parametrized: `Harness [steps [seed [popseed [depth width]]]]`). NOTE the earlier default golden -4507676329811648707 was under an OLD all-same-seed scheme — stale, ignore it.
1. *Replace Conditional with Polymorphism for offspring creation.* `Animal.createNewOffspring` had a `Class classOfAnimal` if/else chain and an unused `motherFoodLevel` param → abstract `Animal createOffspring(Field,Location,boolean,boolean)` implemented per concrete species (mirrors `Plant.createOffspring`).
2. *Pull up duplicated constructor bodies.* The 5 near-identical species ctors now pass their constants to enriched `Prey`/`Predator` super-ctors that do the stat-assignment + age/food init. Prey ctor takes a `newbornFoodFraction` (added `NEWBORN_FOOD_FRACTION` consts: Zebra/Giraffe 0.25, Lemur 0.5); Predator ctor keeps the random newborn food (`rand.nextDouble()/5.5`). Public concrete ctor signatures unchanged.
3. *Extract Method on `Animal.act()`* (was ~85 lines) → `updateInfectionState()`/`tryToCatchDisease()`/`tryToBreed()`/`move()`, exact RNG-call order preserved (short-circuits matter, e.g. `surroundingsInfected() && rand.nextDouble()...`).
4. *Removed dead code in `Animal.setDead()`*: the `if (class==Lion||Cheetah) location=null;` block is unreachable-effect (location already nulled above).
5. *Extract duplicated neighbour iteration.* `Animal.breed()` and `surroundingsInfected()` both hand-rolled the same `adjacentLocations`+Iterator walk → shared `private List<Animal> getAdjacentAnimals()` (for-each, collects non-null neighbours). RNG-safe: `adjacentLocations()` shuffles via Field.rand and is still called exactly once per method call, same order; breed still draws `rand.nextInt(maxLitterSize)` per same-species male in shuffled order (last wins), surroundingsInfected still early-returns on first infected. Swapped unused `import java.util.Iterator` for `ArrayList`. Also incidentally removed breed's redundant 3×-getObjectAt-per-cell.
6. *Tidy remaining model utilities.* `Weather.updateWeather()`: instance-access-to-static-enum `currentWeather.Clear/.Sunny` → `WeatherType.Clear/.Sunny`. `Plant`: `createOffspring` collapsed to one-line `return new Plant(...)`, populate's unused-counter `for(int b=0; free.size()>0; b++)` → `while(!free.isEmpty())`, removed unused `import java.util.Iterator`.

7. *`Simulator.populate()` table-driven.* Replaced the creation-probability if/else-if chain + redundant identity casts `(Lion) new Lion(...)` with a `private record SpeciesSpawn(double creationProbability, BiFunction<Field,Location,Animal> spawner)` + `static final List<SpeciesSpawn> SPECIES_SPAWNS` (5 entries, priority order) and a `for(SpeciesSpawn s: SPECIES_SPAWNS){ if(rand.nextDouble()<=s.creationProbability()){ animal=s.spawner().apply(field,location); break; } }` loop. The for-loop-with-break is the exact desugaring of the cascading chain → same nextDouble draw count/order per cell. Added `import java.util.function.BiFunction`. Adding a species is now one table line.
   *Verification (Simulator is Swing-view-coupled so the model fingerprint harness can't call it):* built a separate driver that allocates a Simulator via `sun.misc.Unsafe.allocateInstance` (skips the JFrame-building ctor — works in Java 21 WITHOUT --add-opens), reflectively sets `field`/`animals`/`plants`, invokes the private `populate()`, and FNV-fingerprints species-per-cell. With a deterministic test-double `Randomizer.getRandom()` returning `new Random(4242)`, baseline (git 298c765 Simulator.java) vs refactored both gave FP=8100322877308688392 (1351 animals/5400 plants, 60×90), stable across runs. Model harness (4 configs) unchanged. Driver/sources under /tmp/popverify.

8. *Remove dead code + simplify getTimeString.* Deleted 5 genuinely-uncalled methods (grep-confirmed zero callers): `Field.randomAdjacentLocation(Location)`, `Field.place(Object,int,int)` overload, `GridSpace.getAnimal()`, `GridSpace.getPlant()`, `Simulator.delay(int)`. Simplified `SimulatorView.getTimeString()`'s nested if/else to `String.format("%02d:00 ", Time.getTime())` (verified identical over all 24 hour values via /tmp/timecheck). Model harness (4 configs) + populate driver (FP=8100322877308688392) both unchanged. NOTE left untouched: `Field.place(Object,Location)`'s `if(gridSpace==null){gridSpace=new GridSpace();}` branch is dead AND latently buggy (never writes the new GridSpace back to the array) — but cells are always cleared() first so it never triggers; leaving as a known latent quirk.

9. *Enum-based `Species` single source of truth.* New `Species.java` enum (LION,CHEETAH,ZEBRA,GIRAFFE,LEMUR in population-priority order) holds per-species: `speciesClass()`, `creationProbability()`, `fillColor()`, `textColor()`, `spawn(field,location)` (BiFunction). Replaced in `Simulator`: the 5 `*_CREATION_PROBABILITY` constants, the round-7 `SpeciesSpawn` record + `SPECIES_SPAWNS` list, and the 5 hardcoded animal `view.setColor(...)` calls. populate() now loops `Species.values()`; constructor colour setup loops `Species.values()` then one explicit `view.setColor(Plant.class, GREEN, BLACK)` (Plant is not part of the animal spawn cascade, kept separate). Removed Simulator's `import java.util.function.BiFunction`. Adding a species = one enum constant. Verified: populate driver byte-identical to pristine baseline (FP=8100322877308688392); standalone ColorCheck confirms enum class→(fill,text) data == original hardcoded mappings; model harness unchanged. **One cosmetic change disclosed to user:** the GUI legend (classKey panel) order changed from [Zebra,Giraffe,Lemur,Lion,Cheetah,Plant] to [Lion,Cheetah,Zebra,Giraffe,Lemur,Plant] because colour setup now iterates priority order — colours-per-species unchanged, simulation unaffected (couldn't satisfy both the populate priority order AND the old legend order with one declaration order; chose the behaviourally-significant one).

10. *Replace Magic Number with Named Constant (polish).* Named the inline rule probabilities: Animal `OVERCROWDING_DEATH_PROBABILITY=0.3`, `IMMUNITY_LOSS_DIVISOR=15`, `OFFSPRING_IMMUNITY_INHERITANCE_PROBABILITY=0.15`, `OFFSPRING_IMMUNITY_LOSS_PROBABILITY=0.9`; Predator `NIGHT_ACTIVITY_CHANCE=0.25`, `FOG_ACTIVITY_CHANCE=0.50`. Left the disease field initialisers (already assigned to named fields) and ctor `/5.5` alone to avoid churn. Model harness (4 configs) unchanged.

**R008 status / remaining targets:** MODEL layer (Animal hierarchy, Weather, Plant), `Simulator.populate()`, species metadata (Species enum), dead code, and magic-number naming all done. Codebase is in good shape; 10 verified refactor rounds completed. FURTHER PASSES ARE POLISH/CHURN — told the user the substantive work is complete and recommended stopping unless there's a specific goal. Don't invent low-value churn just to keep going. Lower-value remaining smells: `Class objectType` dispatch through Field/GridSpace (works fine as a generic 2-layer grid; refactor would be churn, not clearly better); GridSpace.getObject/clear and setObject still instanceof/Class-dispatch. Remaining smell deliberately NOT done (high-risk/invasive): the pervasive `Class objectType` threading through `Field`/`GridSpace` (getObjectAt/clear/getObject/setObject dispatch on Animal.class vs Plant.class). An enum-based `Species` single-source-of-truth (like the R004 variant) would be the big structural win but spans Simulator+SimulatorView and is RNG-order-sensitive in populate. Verification toolkit available: (a) model fingerprint harness /tmp/harness/Harness.java (reflectively seeds the 3 static rands); (b) Unsafe-based populate driver /tmp/popverify (real Simulator.populate without the view).

**Known latent bugs (left unfixed — would change simulation output):** `Consumer.maxSustenanceLevel` shadows `Actor.maxSustenanceLevel` and stays 0; `Consumer.eat()` uses `consumptionWorth` instead of `actorConsumptionWorth` for leftover food; `Disease.STEPS_BEFORE_DEATH` is `static` (shared across all diseases).

**Variants differ — the `module_java` worktrees are NOT all the same code.** The `R004_module_java` worktree uses a different hierarchy: `Actor` (interface) + abstract `Organism` → `Animal`/`Plant` → concrete species (Deer/Coyote/Wolf/Eagle/Mouse/Grass/Hunter), Swing-only `SimulatorView`, no JavaFX at all (`javac *.java` compiles cleanly with no stubs). Here `Randomizer.getRandomSex()` uses the SEEDED `rand.nextBoolean()` (seed=1), so gender IS deterministic and the whole sim is reproducible — different from the Math.random() caveat above. Latent bugs in this variant: `Disease` propagation/lethality are `static` (last-created disease's values shared by all); `Hunter.alive` is `static` (shared across hunters). Verify behaviour-preserving refactors with a headless harness that mirrors `Simulator.populate()`/`simulateOneStep()` driving the real model classes and FNV-hashes per-step class counts (the view blocks running `Simulator` directly — it constructs a `JFrame`, which HANGS in this no-display env, not just throws). In R004 the model now lives in a view-free `SimulationEngine` (extracted from `Simulator`), so harnesses can drive `new SimulationEngine(160,240); engine.reset(); engine.step()` directly instead of copying the loop.

**Weather determinism — FIXED (was a cross-JVM non-determinism bug).** Historically `Weather.changeWeather()` did `new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList(WeatherType...)).toArray()[randomInt]`; HashSet-of-enum iteration order depends on identity hashCodes, which differ between JVM processes, so the same seed produced different weather sequences (and thus different whole-sim output) in different processes — fingerprints were only comparable WITHIN one process. This was fixed (with the user's explicit OK to change output) by selecting from `WeatherType.values()` (fixed declaration order [RAINING,SUNNY,CLOUDY]); `weatherList`/`addWeatherList` removed. RNG consumption is unchanged (still one `rand.nextInt(3)` per change) and the distribution stays uniform, so only the deterministic trace is pinned — now stable across JVMs. In this env the unperturbed run already iterated in declaration order, so the canonical fingerprint (engine harness, 160x240, 150 steps, position-sensitive sig) is **-2184605646102145951** and is now identical across processes. Verified by perturbing the identity-hashCode PRNG (`System.identityHashCode(new Object())` ×N before building the engine): pre-fix N=0/7/100/5000 gave 4 different fingerprints; post-fix all give -2184605646102145951. Consequence for future work: cross-process fingerprint comparison is now VALID. Still use a POSITION-sensitive signature (class+diseased per cell), not counts-only.

**Disease per-instance rates — FIXED (was `static`).** `Disease.PROPAGATION_RATE`/`LETHALITY_RATE` were `static`, so every disease returned the LAST-created instance's rates (≈17 distinct diseases exist right after populate but all behaved as one). Made them instance fields `propagationRate`/`lethalityRate` (and renamed `PROPAGATION_MODE`→`propagationMode`; `rand` is now a local in the default ctor). User OK'd the output change. Disease CONSTRUCTION RNG is unchanged (same 3 draws/ctor), so populate creates byte-identical diseases; divergence begins at STEP 1's propagation-death check (17 diseased orgs now use their own rates 0.0017–0.50 instead of all using the last-created ~0.50), cascading to a fully different but deterministic trace. After both fixes the canonical engine-harness fingerprint (160x240, 150 steps, position-sensitive) is **-8012133067710255676** (was -2184605646102145951 pre-Disease-fix). No known latent simulation bugs remain after this.

**Species registry (R004).** A `Species` enum is now the single source of truth for per-species metadata: actor class, display name, GUI colour, default creation probability, `maxCount` cap, and a spawner lambda — in population-priority order. `SimulationEngine` derives populate order/probabilities/spawners from it (hunter cap generalised to `Species.maxCount()` enforced via a static `spawnedCounts` EnumMap, never reset → same global-across-resets behaviour as the old static `hunterCount`). `SimulatorView` builds its population checkboxes/colours/tooltips by looping `Species.values()` (no per-species hardcoding); `SimulationInfo` keeps only the `HIGHEST_*` testing fields (ALL_ACTORS/DEFAULT_COLOR_MAP removed). Adding a species = one enum constant. Model behaviour verified unchanged (fingerprint still -8012133067710255676); GUI is reasoning-verified only (JFrame can't run here). Note: the checkbox column order changed to enum order and `setColorsByCheckBox` now includes Mouse (the old hardcoded array omitted it).

Done — fourth refactoring complete.

## Consolidated `SimulatorView`'s button listeners

The three control buttons (4000 Steps / Reset / One Step) each had a verbose anonymous `ActionListener` repeating the same shape: check whether any conflicting operation is already running, bail if so, otherwise spawn a new thread and stash it in a field for future liveness checks.

**Changes:**
- Extracted two small, single-responsibility static helpers:
  - `anyAlive(Thread...)` — the guard (true if any passed thread is non-null and running)
  - `startThread(Runnable)` — launches a task on a new thread and returns it
- Converted the three anonymous `ActionListener` classes into lambdas that use those helpers.
- Removed the dead `setInfoText(String)` method (grep-confirmed zero callers).

The per-button semantics are preserved **exactly** — each button still guards on the same set of threads and assigns the same field, including the existing quirk that "4000 Steps" and "One Step" don't check the reset thread while "Reset" checks all three.

Net: ~31 lines of repetitive listener boilerplate became ~17 lines of intent-revealing code, plus two reusable helpers.

## Verification
Compiles cleanly. The class count went from 32 to **29** — confirming the three anonymous `SimulatorView$1/$2/$3` classes are eliminated (lambdas compile to `invokedynamic`, not separate class files). Behavior-preserving by construction; this is GUI code that can't be exercised headlessly here, but the transformation is mechanically equivalent.

## Noted for a future pass (left untouched)
While reviewing I confirmed three trivially-dead imports — unused `import java.awt.Color` in both `Counter.java` and `FieldStats.java`, and `import java.awt.event.*` in `SimulatorView` (now unused after the lambda conversion). I deliberately left these to keep this round focused; happy to sweep them next.

Want me to continue with another pass (e.g. that import sweep, or something more substantive), or stop and commit here?
